argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical defense of Jamesian pragmatism against the charge of incoherence
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate - premises are embedded in narrative but recoverable

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High - engages with strongest objections and offers nuanced responses
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High - all moves directly address the coherence/arbitrariness challenge
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate - relies on pragmatist commitments that critics may reject

distinctions_drawn: tolerance as meta-principle vs. tolerance as practical virtue
explicit_definitions_given: Coherence = procedural consistency, not logical consistency
Tolerance = methodological disposition, not transcendent law

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Reframes the objection as category mistake; accepts incompleteness but denies incoherence
objections_raised: No definitive answer to moral conflicts

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, hypothetical examples, pragmatic thought experiments

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Moral conflict, pluralism, tolerance, practical reason

structural_organization.structure_type: Problem-solution with dialectical escalation: thesis → critique → defense → resolution

summary_of_core_decisions: The text defends James by shifting the criterion of coherence from logical consistency to methodological efficacy, redefining tolerance as a practical tool rather than a foundational axiom, and distinguishing between a definition of good and a rule for resolving conflicts.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Defense of a position against objections
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low - ends with strong affirmation of wisdom over incoherence
